readings_chosen: Sentence 1: 'the morning's routine'. Readings: (i) 'morning' is a time word with no form and the thing is only 'routine'; (ii) the words name which routine and stay inside the thing's name. Chosen: (ii); the time word is put in the bin as well, and no claim about when is written.

Sentence 1: 'in her notebook'. Readings: (i) the place the description sits in; (ii) the medium the description was made in; (iii) the notebook as what the description went to. Chosen: none of these has a form, so the whole phrase goes to the bin; the notebook keeps line book.

Sentence 2: 'from the water tank first to the soil trays last'. Readings: (i) the water tank and the soil trays are the sources of the first and last listed samples, so the items are unnamed samples; (ii) they name the first and last items in their own right. Chosen: (ii), so that no sample thing is invented; lines first and last are marked filled in because the naming of the items is my part.

Sentence 2: 'in the order she had tested them'. Readings: (i) the listing's order is the testing's order (line order), with the testing as a happening of its own (line test); (ii) a Link line from list to test; (iii) a Depends line. Chosen: (i); a Link needs a stated result of the testing and there is none, and Depends is for plans.

Sentence 3: 'the temperature of the incubator'. Readings: (i) the temperature is the thing recorded (line temp), with the incubator inside its name; (ii) the incubator is the thing recorded, plus a fact that it has a temperature. Chosen: (i), the text's own object of 'recorded'.

Sentence 3: 'at nine, at noon, and at four'. Readings: (i) three recordings at three times; (ii) one record holding three readings. Chosen: neither can be written (times, amounts and counts are outside the language); line record is one happening and the phrase goes to the bin.

Sentences 1, 4, 5: the attributions to the notebook ('described ... in her notebook', 'The notebook also described', 'she noted that'). Readings: (i) bin the attribution words and keep only the content TOLD, as the guide's 'the account says' example does; (ii) keep the acts of writing as happenings in the actual ledger and put the written content TOLD in notebook_world. Chosen: (ii), because these sentences also assert things the technician did; the attributions are carried by the TOLD standing of the written content.

Sentence 4: 'the new labels the supplier had sent, each printed in blue ink'. Readings: (i) 'new' and 'printed in blue ink' are the notebook's described content and stand TOLD; (ii) they are the narrator's own descriptions and stand in the actual ledger. Chosen: (i), since what a note says is TOLD. The labels' existence and the supplier's sending stay in the actual ledger (supplier and send are GIVEN, from the relative clause).

Sentence 4: 'each printed in blue ink'. Readings: (i) each label carries printing made in blue ink by an unnamed printer, so it is a happening; (ii) each label's ink is blue, a plain description. Chosen: (ii), written as one fact about the labels as a whole with 'each' binned; no printer is invented and 'printed' is not written as a happening.
Sentence 5: 'noted'. Readings: (i) wrote down in the notebook; (ii) noticed and took in. Chosen: (i), from 'At the end of the page'.

Sentence 5: the thing 'noted' takes. Readings: (i) name it after the content (cleaning_record); (ii) use the fume cupboard as the thing noted. Chosen: (i); lines entry and note are filled in and say which part is mine.

Happenings in the file. Readings: (i) encode each happening as holds(verb(dober, thing)); (ii) give a happening line only the line(id) fact. Chosen: (i), because the guide's predicate list has no predicate for a happening and holds(...) is the only place a verb's doing can be read.
